#!/usr/bin/env bash
# run trigger/pc gating: --trigger / --pc-start / --pc-end are the hybrid ROI
# delimiters. fast/cycle used to silently IGNORE them -- a user asking for a
# pc window got a whole-program cycle figure with no warning. They are now
# rejected (rc 2) on any model except hybrid.
#
#   1. cycle/fast + --trigger          -> usage error (rc 2)
#   2. cycle/fast + --pc-end           -> usage error (rc 2)
#   3. cycle/fast + --pc-start         -> usage error (rc 2)
#   5. hybrid + --trigger pc + pc-*    -> never gated (reaches the ELF check)
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-rt_c_hello}"
hybrid_resolve_paths
ENGINE="${ENGINE:-vsim:ax45mpv_premium}"
MISSING=/no/such/file.elf

# 1-3. fast/cycle reject the hybrid-only ROI knobs (real ELF: pre-gate these
# ran the whole program and returned 0; the gate must now turn them into rc 2).
expect 2 'trigger applies only to --mode hybrid' \
  "$BIN" run --mode cycle --engine "$ENGINE" --trigger pc \
  --pc-start 0x100074 --pc-end 0x100080 "$VSIM_ELF"
expect 2 'trigger applies only to --mode hybrid' \
  "$BIN" run --mode fast --trigger marker "$VSIM_ELF"
expect 2 'pc-end applies only to --mode hybrid' \
  "$BIN" run --mode cycle --engine "$ENGINE" --pc-end 0x100080 "$VSIM_ELF"
expect 2 'pc-start applies only to --mode hybrid' \
  "$BIN" run --mode cycle --engine "$ENGINE" --pc-start 0x100074 "$VSIM_ELF"
expect 2 'pc-start applies only to --mode hybrid' \
  "$BIN" run --mode fast --pc-start 0x100074 "$VSIM_ELF"
ok "fast/cycle reject --trigger/--pc-start/--pc-end"

# 5. hybrid is the home of these flags: never gated, reaches the ELF check.
expect 2 'ELF not found' \
  "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger pc --engine "$ENGINE" \
  --pc-start 0x100074 --pc-end 0x100080 "$MISSING"
ok "hybrid --trigger pc not gated"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# PC-trigger contract: the drained resume PC equals the --pc-start boundary.
#
# The drain callback fires BEFORE the trigger insn executes, so the captured
# state is pre-execution. A marker is an architectural NOP and may be skipped
# (resume at vaddr+size), but a pc boundary is real user code: if the plugin
# reports vaddr+size, the boundary insn executes on NEITHER leg (e.g. a
# skipped vsetivli leaves vtype.vill set and the vsim window faults on the
# first vector op). The plugin must report the boundary's own vaddr so the
# insn runs inside the measured window.
#
# Required environment (auto-detected with sensible defaults):
#   VSIM_QEMU    qemu-system-riscv64
#   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so
#   VSIM_ELF     any fixture with a `main` symbol (default: vplat_hello.elf)

set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-vplat_hello}"
hybrid_resolve_paths

NM="${NM:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}}"
command -v "${NM:-nm}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || NM=nm
ENTER_HEX=$("$NM" "$VSIM_ELF" | awk '$3 == "main" { print $1; exit }')
[ -n "$ENTER_HEX" ] || { echo "FAIL[pc_trigger_resume_pc]: no main in $VSIM_ELF"; exit 1; }
ENTER=$(printf '0x%x' "0x$ENTER_HEX")

SHARED_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-pcresume-shared.XXXXXX)
STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
QEMU_LOG=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_QEMU" "$QEMU_LOG"' EXIT
truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"

set +e
"$VSIM_QEMU" \
  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  -nographic \
  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=$STATE_QEMU,enter_pc=$ENTER" \
  </dev/null >"$QEMU_LOG" 2>&1
RC=$?
set -e

if [ "$RC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[pc_trigger_resume_pc]: expected QEMU exit=200 on drain, got $RC"
  tail -5 "$QEMU_LOG"
  exit 1
fi
if ! grep -q "drained state to .* (pc=$ENTER)" "$QEMU_LOG"; then
  echo "FAIL[pc_trigger_resume_pc]: resume PC != pc-start boundary $ENTER:"
  grep "drained state" "$QEMU_LOG" || tail -5 "$QEMU_LOG"
  exit 1
fi
echo "[pc_trigger_resume_pc] PASS: drain resumes at the boundary insn ($ENTER)"

# Shared path resolution for the top-level e2e harness + drivers.
# Sourced (not executed). Provides:
#   TOP_ROOT                  - absolute path of the repo root
#   hybrid_resolve_paths()    - sets VSIM_BIN, VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN,
#                               VSIM_ELF from TOP_ROOT (unless already
#                               exported by caller) and exits 77 (CTest
#                               skip) if any artifact is missing. Reads
#                               FIXTURE for the VSIM_ELF default.

TESTS_LIB_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
TOP_ROOT=$(cd -- "$TESTS_LIB_DIR/../.." && pwd)

if [ -z "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" ] && [ -f "$TOP_ROOT/config.env" ]; then
  . "$TOP_ROOT/config.env"
fi

hybrid_resolve_paths() {
  VSIM_BIN="${VSIM_BIN:-${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-$TOP_ROOT/verilator/build}/sim_ax45mpv_premium}"
  VSIM_QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-$TOP_ROOT/build/qemu}/qemu-system-riscv64}"
  VSIM_PLUGIN="${VSIM_PLUGIN:-$TOP_ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so}"
  VSIM_ELF="${VSIM_ELF:-$TOP_ROOT/tests/fixtures/${FIXTURE}.elf}"
  for f in "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_QEMU" "$VSIM_PLUGIN" "$VSIM_ELF"; do
    if [ ! -e "$f" ]; then
      echo "skip: $f not built; run 'source ./setup.sh' and 'make -C tests/fixtures'"
      exit 77
    fi
  done
}
=== tests/lib/log.sh (expect/ok/fail) ===
# Shared status printers for test scripts. Sourced (not executed).
#
#   fail <msg...>          -> "[FAIL] <msg>" on stderr, exit 1
#   ok   <msg...>          -> "[ok] <msg>" on stdout
#   expect <rc> <re> CMD.. -> run CMD, fail unless it exits <rc> and its
#                             combined output matches the <re> regex
#
# These patterns were duplicated byte-identically across many test scripts.
# Source via:   . "$SCRIPT_DIR/<rel>/lib/log.sh"

fail() { echo "[FAIL] $*" >&2; exit 1; }
ok()   { echo "[ok] $*"; }

expect() {
  local want="$1" re="$2"; shift 2
  local out rc
  out=$("$@" 2>&1 </dev/null); rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -eq "$want" ] || fail "rc=$rc want $want for [$*]: $out"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq "$re" || fail "missing /$re/ for [$*]: $out"
}

# Repo root, derived from this lib's own location (tests/lib/ -> ../..).
_LIB_ROOT=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)

# cfg_val KEY -> the value of KEY in the repo-root config.env ("" if absent).
# A lightweight read so a test runs without a prior `source ./setup.sh`.
cfg_val() { grep -oP "$1=\\K.*" "$_LIB_ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '"' | head -1; }

# The external vsim build dir (the sim_* binaries), the way the driver resolves
# it: VSIM_BIN_DIR env, then config.env, then the legacy in-tree build dir.
vsim_bin_dir() {
  if [ -n "${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"; return; fi
  local v; v=$(cfg_val VSIM_BIN_DIR)
  [ -n "$v" ] && printf '%s\n' "$v" || printf '%s\n' "$_LIB_ROOT/verilator/build"
}

# hybrid trigger/pc gating: --mode hybrid REQUIRES --trigger (marker|pc), and
# --trigger pc REQUIRES both --pc-start and --pc-end (a symbol name or 0x
# address, resolved against the ELF .symtab). There is no silent marker
# default -- an unmarked ELF run without a trigger used to fast-forward the
# whole program and surface only as a cryptic drain-exit mismatch.
#
#   1. hybrid, no --trigger                  -> usage error (rc 2)
#   2. hybrid --trigger pc, no --pc-*        -> usage error (rc 2)
#   3. hybrid --trigger pc, only --pc-start  -> usage error (rc 2)
#   4. hybrid --trigger pc, unreadable ELF   -> resolve error surfaces (rc 2)
#   5. hybrid --trigger bogus                -> unknown trigger (rc 2)

ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

  "$BIN" run --mode hybrid "$ELF"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# PC-trigger contract: the drained resume PC equals the --pc-start boundary.
#
# The drain callback fires BEFORE the trigger insn executes, so the captured
# state is pre-execution. A marker is an architectural NOP and may be skipped
# (resume at vaddr+size), but a pc boundary is real user code: if the plugin
# reports vaddr+size, the boundary insn executes on NEITHER leg (e.g. a
# skipped vsetivli leaves vtype.vill set and the vsim window faults on the
# first vector op). The plugin must report the boundary's own vaddr so the
# insn runs inside the measured window.
#
# Required environment (auto-detected with sensible defaults):
#   VSIM_QEMU    qemu-system-riscv64
#   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so
#   VSIM_ELF     any fixture with a `main` symbol (default: vplat_hello.elf)

set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-vplat_hello}"
hybrid_resolve_paths

NM="${NM:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}}"
command -v "${NM:-nm}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || NM=nm
ENTER_HEX=$("$NM" "$VSIM_ELF" | awk '$3 == "main" { print $1; exit }')
[ -n "$ENTER_HEX" ] || { echo "FAIL[pc_trigger_resume_pc]: no main in $VSIM_ELF"; exit 1; }
ENTER=$(printf '0x%x' "0x$ENTER_HEX")

SHARED_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-pcresume-shared.XXXXXX)
STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
QEMU_LOG=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_QEMU" "$QEMU_LOG"' EXIT
truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"

set +e
"$VSIM_QEMU" \
  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  -nographic \
  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=$STATE_QEMU,enter_pc=$ENTER" \
  </dev/null >"$QEMU_LOG" 2>&1
RC=$?
set -e

if [ "$RC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[pc_trigger_resume_pc]: expected QEMU exit=200 on drain, got $RC"
  tail -5 "$QEMU_LOG"
  exit 1
fi
if ! grep -q "drained state to .* (pc=$ENTER)" "$QEMU_LOG"; then
  echo "FAIL[pc_trigger_resume_pc]: resume PC != pc-start boundary $ENTER:"
  grep "drained state" "$QEMU_LOG" || tail -5 "$QEMU_LOG"
  exit 1
fi
echo "[pc_trigger_resume_pc] PASS: drain resumes at the boundary insn ($ENTER)"
